items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: the second tune I ever wrote lyrics to was Keith Jarrett’s “Lucky Southern” with Airto Moreira was on it, an Airto album.

ctx.x: Well I was aware of, in the sixties I was aware of Stan Getz and Astrud Gilberto and Joao Gilberto and that era of things. But some musicians in Cleveland, Skip Hadden, who now

teaches at Berklee, drums at Berklee, he was very broad and he would bring records by Hermeto Pascoal and when I heard Milton Nascimento and people like that, in the early seventies. And then the second tune I ever wrote lyrics to was Keith Jarrett’s “Lucky Southern” with Airto Moreira was on it, an Airto album. And it was a samba, and there’s another rhythm. The exotic rhythms — I love Brazilian music because, like jazz, it has influences from Africa, they had slavery there and imported a lot of Africans. So…
